summary: Add two exact minimum-side lemmas: a signed path-forest/interval-charge expansion of the dual determinant and an endpoint-defect positive-cell decomposition with a common adjacent-eigenvalue translation speed. Keep determinant orientation and global reflection explicitly open.

node.title: Path-forest expansion of the minimum dual determinant
node.statement: The accepted minimum dual-event matrix, its positive odd-cell blocks, and the alternating transverse event word imply the signed rooted-forest and positive-jump scaled determinant identities stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-FOREST-CHARGE-R36.

node.title: Signed forest and interval-charge formula for the minimum determinant
node.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse common-terminal minimum-law root, put N=n-1 and let H=C P^(-1)C^T-W be the accepted dual negative-edge Schur matrix. There are strictly positive path conductances tau_i and real vertex charges z_i such that H=L_tau+diag(z). If E ranges over retained edge subsets and Comp(E) over their interval components, then det(H)=sum_E (product_(i in E) tau_i) (product_(I in Comp(E)) sum_(j in I)z_j), including det(H)=0. Moreover, for the strictly positive physical event-jump vector v_i=(gamma_(2i+1)-gamma_(2i))/W_i, put q_i=v_i(Hv)_i and e_i=s_(i+1)v_i v_(i+1)>0. Then (product_i v_i^2)det(H) is the same forest polynomial with tau_i replaced by e_i and every interval charge replaced by Q_I=sum_(i in I)q_i. No sign of the interval charges, det(H)>0, reflection symmetry, uniqueness, or existence follows from these identities alone.

node.title: Positive-cell defect decomposition and common translation drift
node.statement: Exact two-frequency propagation on each positive minimum cell, direct low-mode energy jumps at all relay events, and monodromy conjugation under common spatial translation imply the defect and drift identities stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-DEFECT-TRANSLATION-R36.

node.title: Minimum endpoint defect as positive-cell drift and common translation speed
node.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, mu>1, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse equal-norm minimum full-relay root, normalize the low mode by U_t(0)=1, put p=U_t(L), D=p^2-1, and C0=q^2-1>0. For each of the n internal positive cells let 0<theta_a<pi/(mu+1), z_a>0 be its positive low-mode amplitude ratio, k_mu(theta)=sin((mu-1)theta/2)/sin((mu+1)theta/2), and E_mu(theta,z)=(sin(mu theta)^2-sin(theta)^2)(1/k_mu-z)(z-k_mu)/(sin(theta)^2 sin(mu theta)^2). Then k_mu<z_a<1/k_mu and D=(R-1)C0 sum_a Phi_mu(theta_a,z_a), where Phi_mu=(z^2-1)/E_mu and Phi_mu(theta,1/z)=-Phi_mu(theta,z). Strict first-crossing physical positive cells occur with either sign of Phi, so no cellwise fixed-sign conclusion is valid. If all interfaces are translated through the common endpoint material, the adjacent Dirichlet eigenvalues have the same first derivative D/I at a complete equal-norm root. Thus first-order translation cancels from their gap and supplies neither a one-sided sign of D nor global reflection symmetry.

rationale.scope: Both identities cover arbitrary finite contrast, all n>=2, and asymmetric premise-complete transverse minimum roots. Neither signs the physical interval charges or the coupled positive-cell defect sum.
rationale.duplicate_policy: The canonical determinant-parity lemma defines H and calibrates its target sign but contains no rooted-forest or interval-charge expansion. Existing defect and parameter-action claims contain neither this positive-cell Phi decomposition nor the common spatial-translation speed.
rationale.computation_policy: Exact checkers audit algebra and strict local first-crossing witnesses only. No finite search, conditional R14/R17 result, or local cell is used as a universal root theorem or physical counterexample.

ordered_steps: Expand the accepted positive two-by-two odd-cell blocks to write the tridiagonal dual matrix exactly as H=L_tau+diag(z), with tau_i>0 and real charges z_i.

Adjoin a root vertex with formal edge weights z_i. The signed matrix-tree polynomial groups spanning trees by their retained path forest; each interval component contributes the sum of its possible root attachments, proving the rooted-forest formula without a positivity assumption on z.
Use the transverse alternating event signs to define v_i=(gamma_(2i+1)-gamma_(2i))/W_i>0. The exact physical matrix equation gives q_i=v_i(Hv)_i and diagonal congruence gives VHV=L_e+diag(q).
Apply the same forest identity to VHV and use det(VHV)=(product v_i^2)det(H), yielding the interval-charge formula. Stop before asserting a sign, since no premise signs every Q_I.
boundary_cases: For n=2, N=1 and the formula is det(H)=z_1=q_1/v_1^2; no path edge is introduced.
Signed root edges are handled as a polynomial identity, so exact cancellations and det(H)=0 are included without division by H.
Arbitrary asymmetric roots and both reflection orientations are retained; reflection reverses and positively rescales the charges but does not sign them.
No sign is propagated across switch coalescence or a dimension-changing soft-pair limit without rates for v,q,e; the theorem is stated in the premise-complete transverse fixed-dimension scope.

ordered_steps: Solve both constant-coefficient oscillators on a strict internal positive minimum cell. At the two opposite relay rays obtain C0=A^2 E_mu(theta,z) and factor E_mu to prove k_mu(theta)<z<1/k_mu(theta).

Derive rather than assume the endpoint defect: low-mode energy is constant on cells and jumps by Delta rho_j U(t_j)^2. Summing the alternating minimum jumps from slopes 1 to p gives D=(R-1) sum_j (-1)^j U(t_j)^2, then pair the positive-cell endpoints and substitute C0=A^2E_mu.

Use z^2E_mu(theta,1/z)=E_mu(theta,z) to obtain the reciprocal oddness of Phi. Exact mu=2, theta=pi/6, z=1/2 and z=2 propagations certify strict first crossings with opposite Phi signs, refuting only a cellwise fixed-sign mechanism.
Translate all switches through the common endpoint material. Monodromy conjugation M_h=T_R(-h)MT_R(h) and the differentiated Dirichlet condition give lambda'(0)=(p^2-1)/I.

Normalize the adjacent high mode and use equal norm plus the terminal energy relation to obtain the same D/I speed for both eigenvalues. Hence the first derivative of the gap cancels and no sign or reflection conclusion is drawn.
boundary_cases: The sum has n terms for every n>=2 and retains arbitrary asymmetric positive-cell phases and amplitudes.
At z=1 the local drift vanishes but the cell remains strict; this gives no information about other cells.
The formula uses the factor R-1 without dividing by it in a claimed R=1 theorem, so no uniform nonzero limit as R decreases to 1 is asserted.
Endpoint cells are absent from the paired sum but remain in the full-root closure; the exact local opposite-sign cells are not claimed to close globally or form a counterexample.
First-order translation is exhausted; no second-variation sign, one-sided D inequality, determinant orientation, or global reflection theorem is asserted.
